problem: Open-vocabulary grounding requires fine-grained vision-language alignment without dense supervision, but existing methods either sacrifice expressiveness with global embeddings or demand explicit token-level labels.
approach: ExpAlign uses a theoretically grounded MIL formulation with an Expectation Alignment Head that performs soft pooling over token-region similarities, paired with energy-based multi-scale consistency regularization including contrastive and geometry-aware objectives.
contribution: ExpAlign achieves 36.2 AP_r on LVIS minival, outperforming comparable baselines on open-vocabulary detection and zero-shot instance segmentation while remaining lightweight and inference-efficient.

problem: Full-body 3D human motion recovery from head-mounted signals suffers from local joint reconstruction errors due to reliance on global distribution matching in diffusion-based methods.
approach: MotionGRPO frames diffusion sampling as a Markov decision process optimized via Group Relative Policy Optimization, using a hybrid reward combining learned perceptual models and explicit joint constraints, with a noise-injection strategy to increase sample diversity.
contribution: MotionGRPO achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3D motion recovery from egocentric sensors with improved visual fidelity and addresses the vanishing gradient problem from limited intra-group sample diversity.

problem: Understanding how neural language models learn context-free grammars and develop syntactic competence remains unclear, particularly regarding interactions between hierarchical grammatical substructures.
approach: The work extends neural language modeling theory by defining subgrammars and proving that modeling loss decomposes linearly over top-level subgrammars and recursively into irreducible components, with empirical analysis of subgrammar pretraining and learned representations.
contribution: Proves fundamental theorems connecting language modeling loss to CFG substructure; shows parametrized models learn subgrammars in parallel and that pretraining improves representations for small models but with limited performance gains.

problem: Large diffusion vision-language models suffer from repetitive generation and degraded visual grounding during long-form generation due to mask token prior drift and misalignment between positional attention and iterative unmasking.
approach: Proposes training-free Mask Prior Suppression and Monotonic RoPE Scaling to address mask token representation drift and restore proper positional attention alignment during decoding without modifying model weights.
contribution: Achieves improvements on general multimodal benchmarks and visual grounding tasks with robust gains on long-form description generation via lightweight, plug-and-play defenses that generalize across diverse LDVLM architectures.

problem: Visual-language-action models are limited by scarce real-world robot datasets and misalignment between separately trained Latent Action Models and VLAs, leading to poor generalization.
approach: LARA jointly optimizes LAMs and VLAs through representation alignment, enabling LAMs to learn from action trajectories while VLAs are regularized by forward dynamics to reduce hallucinations, as a plug-and-play framework.
contribution: Achieves approximately 10% improvement on simulation benchmarks, ~5% on mixed, and ~15% on real-world manipulation tasks compared to baselines, with versatility across pre-training and post-training enhancement scenarios.

problem: Existing LLM unlearning methods fail to achieve true forgetting in practice; sensitive information reliably resurfaces under probabilistic decoding despite appearing unlearned under deterministic evaluation.
approach: Introduces leak@k metric to quantify reappearance of forgotten knowledge under k-sampling and proposes RULE (Robust Unlearning under LEak@k) algorithm to address persistent knowledge leakage across standard benchmarks.
contribution: Demonstrates that only limited forgetting is achieved by SOTA unlearning; leak@k metric provides first large-scale systematic evaluation; RULE achieves no information leakage on TOFU benchmark with many generation samples.

problem: Claims that LLM evaluators are narcissistic self-raters may be confounded by evaluator quality differences rather than true model preference for own outputs.
approach: Directly compares judge voting distributions for self-evaluation versus external model evaluation, using this baseline to separate narcissism from evaluator quality effects, with entropy analysis of voting patterns.
contribution: Shows only 51% of prior findings retain significance against the evaluator quality baseline, covering 89.6% of reported self-preference probability mass, suggesting confounds in previous narcissism claims.

problem: Deploying LLMs on untrusted hardware risks model weight extraction and unauthorized replication while existing obfuscation schemes face tradeoffs between security guarantees and inference efficiency.
approach: SLIM leverages LLM's iterative structure to cascade transformed representations through obfuscated layers with minimal TEE interactions, using T-Way Mixing with block-diagonal Householder matrices and random permutations.
contribution: Provides robust security guarantees with up to 13.80× speedup over prior obfuscation schemes while preserving fidelity on TEE-based inference.

problem: RAG systems are vulnerable to poisoning attacks at low corruption rates and existing attacks lack stealth, allowing reliable detection and mitigation.
approach: Formalizes stealth via distinguishability-based security game and proposes analyzing LLM attention weights to flag anomalous passages; introduces Normalized Passage Attention Score (NPAS) and Attention-Variance Filter (AV Filter).
contribution: AV Filter improves robustness by up to ~20% over baseline defenses; adaptive attacks achieve 35% success rate, demonstrating both defensive gains and remaining challenges in achieving true attack stealth.

problem: Balancing exploration and exploitation in two-player games remains challenging; existing policy optimization methods lack clear convergence guarantees and stable training dynamics in game-theoretic settings.
approach: Revisits policy optimization with reverse KL and entropy regularization in two-player zero-sum games; provides convergence analysis for normal-form and finite-length games with practical model-free algorithm.
contribution: Demonstrates superior training efficiency compared to existing methods across five board games (Animal Shogi, Gardner Chess, Go, Hex, Othello) with novel convergence guarantees.

problem: Diffusion models face inverse correlation between likelihood optimization and perceptual sample quality, limiting balanced performance on both density estimation and generation.
approach: Proposes Rényi diffusion model using Rényi divergence for training objectives, yielding generalized score matching with explicit control over sample quality versus distribution coverage tradeoff.
contribution: Achieves improved balance between density estimation and sample generation performance across multiple datasets without modifying model architecture or sampling procedures.

problem: Self-consistency inference for LLMs is expensive and lacks principled understanding of sample efficiency and scaling behavior across datasets.
approach: Provides first comprehensive analysis of SC scaling via mode estimation and voting theory, deriving power law scaling; proposes Blend-ASC using dynamic sample allocation to questions during inference.
contribution: Blend-ASC achieves state-of-the-art sample efficiency with 4.8× fewer samples than vanilla SC on average, is hyperparameter-free, and fits any budget.

problem: Flow-matching policies for offline RL learn irregular and unstable vector fields due to objectives agnostic to global properties of generative paths, hindering performance.
approach: Introduces PDE-regularized Q-Learning (PQL) that imposes principled structure via continuity equation regularization and Beta-distributed timestep sampling strategy focusing on critical trajectory segments.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on challenging offline RL tasks by structuring the entire probability flow, balancing imitation and smoothness.

problem: Understanding how multiple agents or substructures coalesce into coherent entities in neural models and LLMs remains unclear, with implications for alignment.
approach: Develops probabilistic modeling framework where agents are outcome distributions with epistemic utility via log score, using logarithmic pooling for compositions; analyzes LLM personas (Luigi/Waluigi) using tilt-based analysis.
contribution: Proves strict unanimity impossible under linear pooling or binary outcomes but possible with three+ outcomes; formalizes agentic alignment phenomena showing Waluigi emerges as antagonistic counterpart to Luigi.

problem: Multi-modal LLMs show unclear modality preferences that affect decision-making but remain insufficiently explored and difficult to control.
approach: Introduces MC² benchmark with controlled evidence-conflict scenarios; proposes representation engineering method to probe and steer modality preference without fine-tuning.
contribution: Reveals all 20 tested MLLMs demonstrate clear modality preferences statistically associated with downstream task performance; method effectively amplifies preference toward desired direction improving multi-modal tasks.

problem: Reasoning segmentation models suffer from overthinking and produce uniformly verbose reasoning chains regardless of task complexity, reducing efficiency.
approach: PixelThink integrates task difficulty estimation and model uncertainty to regulate reasoning generation via reinforcement learning, learning to compress reasoning length according to scene complexity.
contribution: Improves segmentation performance while reducing inference latency by 30.4% and cutting token usage by 48.2%, demonstrating joint optimization of accuracy and efficiency.

problem: Safety alignment is assumed to operate as a binary threshold but actually exhibits instability where perturbations induce stochastic refusal, enabling undetected jailbreak attacks.
approach: Furina develops diagnostic framework combining external and internal signals identifying instability signature of elevated uncertainty with decreased safety activation; constructs fragmented scene-anchored prompts exploiting this.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on HarmBench and MM-SafetyBench, demonstrating uncertainty amplification as transferable mechanism for safety vulnerabilities that detection-based defenses fail against.

problem: Determining task-specific data requirements for language models is difficult in natural language but necessary for understanding learnability of formal structures.
approach: Uses formal languages from probabilistic finite automata as controlled testbed; introduces binning semiring for corpus control and formulates learnability as causal graphical model with decomposed KL divergence metrics.
contribution: Shows correlational evaluation practices are inherently flawed; demonstrates causal analysis enables correct conclusions and serves as warning about correlational pitfalls in language model learnability studies.

problem: AI-generated video detection models generalize poorly across real data with different quality profiles due to quality bias between training real and fake distributions.
approach: Proposes quality-matched real and fake data training and data expansion strategy covering full quality spectrum to learn quality-agnostic detection features.
contribution: Improves generalization across diverse backbones and real data quality variations, enhancing real-world applicability of detection models.

problem: On-policy RL with Gaussian actors and shallow MLPs leads to brittle optimization under noisy gradients and requires conservative policy updates.
approach: Proposes discretized categorical actors representing action dimensions as distributions over discrete bins inducing classification-like objectives; pairs with regularized networks (RN-D) drawing from supervised learning advances.
contribution: Substantially improves continuous-control performance achieving state-of-the-art results within on-policy RL by replacing Gaussian actors.

problem: While supervised fine-tuning limits models to observed reasoning traces, it remains unclear how reinforcement learning enables compositional generalization to unfamiliar recombinations.
approach: Formalizes compositional generalization via Hierarchical Latent Selection Model where traces are generated by cascades of discrete latent variables for reusable modules; proves RL's exploration provides sufficient coverage for latent structure identification.
contribution: Demonstrates RL can extract atomic modules from compound traces and recombine them for novel configurations; shows compound trace training yields stronger generalization than isolated atomic modules.

problem: Hardware-related silent data corruptions during gradient aggregation in distributed training lead to slow or failed convergence without practical fault-tolerance mechanisms.
approach: PAFT formulates errors as gradient inconsistency and introduces dynamic asynchronous parameter synchronization via PAFT-Sync for divergence mitigation and PAFT-Dyn for efficient training overlap.
contribution: Efficiently defends against aggregation errors while maintaining training performance on ResNet, GPT-2, and LLaMA-2 across 4-32 GPUs with standard optimizer support.

problem: Self-supervised learning lacks unifying theoretical framework explaining diverse existing methods and guiding design of new approaches.
approach: Casts SSL as latent distribution matching (LDM): maximizing log-probability under assumed latent model (alignment) while maximizing entropy (uniformity); unifies independent component analysis with contrastive and predictive methods.
contribution: LDM unifies diverse SSL methods and proves identifiable latent representations under mild assumptions; derives nonlinear Kalman-based predictor for high-dimensional timeseries.

problem: As public text data becomes exhausted, machine-generated content increasingly re-enters training corpora, risking performance degradation known as model collapse.
approach: Studies model collapse through language generation in the limit framework introducing replay adversary augmenting streams with generator's past outputs; characterizes when replay fundamentally limits generation.
contribution: Provides learning-theoretic characterization showing replay is benign for uniform generation but creates separations for non-uniform generation; positive results mirror heuristics like data cleaning and watermarking.

problem: Thompson Sampling's mechanism for balancing exploration and exploitation remains unclear despite widespread use and strong empirical performance.
approach: Recasts Thompson Sampling as online optimization algorithm introducing time-invariant regret notion summarizing cumulative regret across horizons; shows TS mimics Bellman-optimal policy with uncertainty regularization.
contribution: Reveals Thompson Sampling's core insight through online optimization lens enabling principled understanding and improvement by comparing against Bellman-optimal benchmark.

problem: Pre-trained vision language models lack good intuitions about physical world and fine-tuned models fail to learn generalizable physical rules.
approach: Tests hypothesis that models need environment interaction via reinforcement learning to learn physical dynamics; evaluates learning through interaction on simulated environments.
contribution: Shows learning from interaction improves within-task performance but fails to produce generalizable physical intuitions; models do not reliably generalize across related tasks sharing visual statistics.

problem: LLMs must align with dynamic scenario-specific behavioral and safety specifications but methods assume static specifications, creating alignment gaps.
approach: Formalizes specification alignment and introduces SpecBench benchmark covering 5 scenarios and 103 specifications; proposes Align3 with hierarchical reflection and revision for reasoning over specification boundaries.
contribution: SpecBench reveals alignment gaps across models; test-time deliberation improves specification alignment; Align3 advances safety-helpfulness frontier with minimal overhead.

problem: LLMs replicate subtle security vulnerabilities from training data; coarse-grained sequence-level optimization fails to address localized nature of security flaws.
approach: Introduces Tree-like Self-Play (TSP) framing secure code generation as fine-grained sequential decision process where model constructs decision tree exploring secure paths and vulnerable variants.
contribution: TSP boosts CodeLlama-7B pass rate to 75.8% surpassing SFT (57.0%); enables robust out-of-distribution generalization reducing unseen CWE vulnerabilities by 24.5% with cross-language transfer.

problem: Dense Transformers couple capacity and computation with every parameter activated per token, creating scaling bottlenecks as models approach trillion-parameter regimes.
approach: cMoLLM reformulates MoE-style mixture layers as variable-kernel dynamic convolutions where experts are kernels and routing implements input-conditioned aggregation via convolutionally gated mixture.
contribution: Improves language modeling perplexity and downstream GLUE/SQuAD accuracy under matched compute with better stream utilization, stable optimization, and favorable scaling vs. ParaScale and AltUp.

problem: Entropy coding in learned image compression becomes the latency bottleneck due to sequential processing, limiting practical deployment.
approach: EF-LIC removes entropy coding entirely using unconstrained vector quantization approaching maximum-entropy bound and context-conditioned autoregressive transforms to reduce inter-dependency.
contribution: Achieves up to 67.86% bitrate reduction over MS-ILLM on Kodak with LPIPS while enabling 3× faster encoding and 5× faster decoding than entropy-coding variants.

problem: Understanding performance gaps between RLHF and DPO remains unclear despite widespread adoption of both preference learning methods.
approach: Provides fine-grained theoretical analysis decomposing gaps into explicit representation gap and implicit representation gap from finite samples; characterizes how model class capacities influence final policy quality.
contribution: Shows RLHF, DPO, or online DPO can outperform depending on model mis-specifications; proves online DPO outperforms both when reward/policy classes are isomorphic; demonstrates RLHF advantage in sample efficiency.

problem: Graph anomaly detection methods focus on anomalies with increased spectral energy variation but miss camouflaged anomalies exhibiting decreased variation.
approach: Proposes node-level spectral energy formulation compatible with message passing; introduces energy-aware graph learning framework modeling spectral shifts via energy-driven message passing for static and temporal graphs.
contribution: Detects camouflaged anomalies previously undetectable; achieves effectiveness and scalability on large-scale benchmarks with unified architecture for temporal settings.

problem: LLMs lack behavioral plasticity to adapt behavioral modes at inference time without retraining; current adaptation methods require extensive fine-tuning.
approach: Reveals LLMs possess intrinsic behavioral plasticity exposable through token-conditional generation; proposes ToCoRL using RL to internalize chameleon-like plasticity via token-conditional prefix conditioning.
contribution: ToCoRL enables precise behavioral control without capability degradation; reasoning models adapt to excel at factual QA previously hindered by step-by-step patterns.

problem: LLM-based embodied agents struggle with perception-reasoning gaps in complex multimodal settings; standalone VLMs often overlook task-critical information.
approach: PRISM couples perception and decision through dynamic question-answer pipeline where LLM critiques VLM descriptions, probes with goal-oriented questions, synthesizing compact task-driven image representations.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art image-based models on ALFWorld and R2R benchmarks with automatic goal-oriented perception pipeline and no handcrafted questions.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models lack structural causal reasoning for counterfactual generation, requiring manual prompt engineering without explicit control.
approach: Causal-Adapter uses structural causal modeling with prompt-aligned injection aligning causal attributes to textual embeddings and conditioned token contrastive loss disentangling factors.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art counterfactual editing on synthetic and real datasets outperforming baselines in effectiveness, composition, realism, and identity preservation.

problem: Evaluating subjective LLM tasks via pairwise comparisons and aggregating to single rankings via Bradley-Terry violates social-choice desiderata and forces heterogeneous preferences into total order.
approach: Applies social choice theory's maximal lotteries to aggregation without imposing ranking assumptions; introduces robust lotteries optimizing worst-case performance under plausible preference shifts.
contribution: Robust lotteries achieve more reliable win rate guarantees across annotator distributions and recover stable top-performing models on large-scale preference datasets.

problem: Large Reasoning Models incur substantial memory and computational overhead from extended reasoning traces; existing KV cache compression methods underperform.
approach: DynTS uses attention map analysis to identify decision-critical tokens steering toward final answer; retains only their KV cache states while evicting redundant entries.
contribution: Surpasses SOTA KV cache compression with 2.6% Pass@1 improvement; reduces inference latency by 1.84-2.62× and peak memory by 3.32-5.73× without compromising reasoning.

problem: Load balancing in distributed MoE inference is critical as skewed routing distributions cause devices with lighter-loaded experts to idle waiting for heavier ones.
approach: EasyBalance performs cross-layer load balancing without expert mapping modifications; schedules cross-layer workloads greedily at each MoE stage deferring remaining workloads.
contribution: Consistently accelerates distributed MoE inference reducing GPU idling by over 40% across different models, tasks, and parallelism configurations.

problem: Evaluating LLM uncertainty at fine-grained levels in long-form generation is challenging due to label imperfections; existing benchmarks rely on fallible external judges.
approach: Introduces SALT benchmark with six procedurally generated tasks featuring single deterministic long textual ground truths enabling unit-level evaluation without external judges.
contribution: Analyzes 50+ LLMs revealing confidence functions dominate uncertainty aspects; shows confidence ranking breaks at atomic level; identifies propagation and degradation as separable error drivers.

problem: Users find it difficult to close gaps between desired images and generated outputs using language prompts alone for personalized image generation.
approach: MultiBO generates K candidate images and obtains multi-choice preferential feedback from users; leverages feedback to guide diffusion model iteratively within B rounds.
contribution: Shows users can effectively guide generative models toward personalized targets through multi-choice feedback; qualitative user scores and quantitative metrics show promising results across five baselines.
